thought.text: The `all.yml` compose scenario would be the entire platform (very heavy). The guide's concrete example is `make up SCENARIO=data_store_backend`. Let me inspect that scenario's full service definition and its runtime dependencies to confirm it's self-contained.

reasoning_content:
The `all.yml` scenario is huge (the entire platform via compose). The debug scenario `data_store_backend` is lighter. Let me check what the debug-data_store_backend scenario actually pulls in — it only includes `services/data_store_backend/service.yml`. Let me look at that service file to understand its dependencies.

The data_store_backend service.yml I saw earlier only defines the `data_store_backend` service with a build, command, volumes, ports, and one env var. It doesn't seem to include postgres or kafka. Wait, let me re-read. The scenario `debug-data_store_backend.yml` only includes `../services/data_store_backend/service.yml`. Let me check whether that service file has dependencies (postgres, kafka) or whether it's standalone.

Actually looking at the service.yml content I retrieved: it only has the `data_store_backend` service. No postgres, no kafka in the include. So `make up SCENARIO=data_store_backend` would run just that one container. But the data_store_backend needs dependencies. Let me check the service file more carefully - maybe it has depends_on and the dependencies are defined elsewhere or it references postgres/kafka that aren't in this scenario.

Wait — the service.yml I cat'd only had `data_store_backend`. Let me look at it fully again and check if there's a `db-init` and depends_on. Actually the scenario only includes service.yml. Let me re-examine. Perhaps data_store_backend is designed to run standalone with just a filesystem store (the description says "Accepts data via POST and persists it to the filesystem"). So it might not need postgres or kafka at all!

Let me check the data_store_backend config to see what it actually needs at runtime.

Actually, this is getting complex. Let me step back and think about the overall strategy.

The task is to "Install the assigned software" — the Smart City Hub platform. The guide (Installation.md) gives two paths:
1. Docker Compose for developing individual services: `make up SCENARIO=data_store_backend`
2. Kubernetes-based full platform: `make local-up`

The full platform (`make local-up`) is extremely resource-hungry (Kafka, NiFi, Keycloak, Harbor, CNPG/PostgreSQL, Grafana, Prometheus, LOKI, Airflow, Mobilizon, Zammad, ThingsBoard, etc.) — that's easily 20+GB of RAM. We only have 7GB RAM + can't enable swap. So the full `make local-up` will not fit in this environment.

The guide itself says "To develop individual services, use Docker Compose to run a service with its dependencies" and gives `make up SCENARIO=data_store_backend` as the concrete example. This is the documented, runnable installation path that fits in the environment.

So my plan:
1. Use the Docker Compose path with the `data_store_backend` scenario (the exact command in the guide).
2. Verify the service comes up and is healthy.

Let me verify the data_store_backend scenario runs. First let me look at the full service.yml and understand dependencies.

Let me re-read the service.yml — I only got a partial. Let me get the full file and check config.
